hero.headline: Postpartum care that helps you feel held, supported and prepared.
hero.text: Cora Perinatal Care offers gentle, practical, and judgment free support starting at pregnancy for the postpartum season, newborn care, feeding, and everything in between.

season.title: Care for the season you are in
season.text: Whether you are preparing for birth, planning for postpartum, or already in the middle of life with a newborn, support should meet you where you are. Cora is here to bring calm, guidance, practical help, and a safe place to ask the questions that come up in real time.

inperson.name: In Person Postpartum Support
inperson.short: Hands on care for families in Massachusetts and New Hampshire who want steady, practical and individualized support after baby arrives.
inperson.p1: Postpartum can feel tender, beautiful, confusing, and exhausting all at once. This is in-home guidance around recovery and rest, newborn care and more.
inperson.p2: Cora supports you without judgment, without pushing one "right way", and without taking over your decisions. The goal is for you to feel more confident and better supported at home.
bullets: In person care in Northern MA and Southern NH
Support with postpartum recovery, healing and mom's overall wellbeing
Guidance with newborn care and infant soothing techniques
Assistance with creating rhythms and routines

classes.name: Birth Preparation, Newborn Care, Lactation, and Postpartum Preparation Classes
classes.short: Private classes and preparation for families who want to feel more informed, supported, and prepared before and after baby arrives.
classes.p1: Thinking ahead to your birth, how to care for your newborn, your lactation journey, or what postpartum may look like can feel overwhelming. Cora offers preparation classes and virtual support to help you approach birth, newborn care, lactation, and the postpartum season with greater clarity and confidence.
classes.p2: These sessions are for families who want information, practical tools, insight, and a space where every question is welcome. The focus isn't on promising perfection at any stage of your journey. It's about helping you feel prepared, informed, and empowered.
classes.p3: Through these classes, you'll gain a better understanding of what to expect, build confidence in making decisions that feel right for you and your family, and learn about the resources and support available to you along the way.

items.title: Birth preparation class - $250
items.intro: This class was designed to help you gain insight on labor and to feel prepared, supported, and empowered for one of life's most transformative experiences.
bullets: The physical and emotional changes your body goes through during labor
What to expect during each stage of the birth process.
items.partners: Partners are strongly encouraged to attend. They will leave with practical tools and hands-on techniques to confidently support you throughout labor, birth, and the early hours after your baby arrives.

items.title: Newborn Care Class - $75
items.intro: Learn what to expect during the first days and weeks of life with your newborn. This class provides a supportive environment where you gain insight into newborn care and learn practical skills, helping you feel more prepared for the transition into parenthood.
bullets: Understanding and responding to your baby's cues
items.partners: Partners are strongly encouraged to attend. Caring for a newborn is a team effort, and this class equips both parents with the knowledge, confidence, and practical skills to care for their baby together.

items.title: Lactation class - $75
items.intro: Gain knowledge on what to expect during the first few days and weeks of your lactation journey. This class was designed to help you feel informed and understand the basics of lactation.
bullets: Milk production and the different phases of breastmilk
How to establish a good latch
items.partners: Partners are strongly encouraged to attend. They play an essential role in supporting breastfeeding, and this class provides practical ways they can encourage and assist you throughout your lactation journey.

items.title: Postpartum preparation class - $75
items.intro: Prepare for the fourth trimester with intention and learn practical ways to build your postpartum plan before your baby arrives. This is a welcoming space to talk openly about the realities of the postpartum period and the transition into parenthood.
bullets: The body's physical and emotional changes
items.partners: Partners are strongly encouraged to attend. Postpartum is a transition for the whole family, and this class gives partners practical tools for supporting recovery and helping create a nurturing environment for the entire family.

virtual.title: Virtual support
virtual.p1: You don't have to navigate postpartum alone. Whether you're looking for guidance through a specific concern or need help troubleshooting a challenge, virtual support allows you to receive personalized care and guidance from wherever you are.
virtual.p2: Our virtual sessions are tailored to what you and your family need in the moment. This support is available whether we've worked together in person before or we're meeting for the first time.
virtual.p3: Whether you need a one-time session for a specific concern or ongoing support as you navigate the postpartum period, virtual care provides a flexible way to stay connected and supported when you need it most.

additional.name: Additional Postpartum Care
additional.short: Thoughtful offerings that honor the body, the family, and the transition into postpartum.
additional.p1: For families who want extra care during this season, Cora also offers placenta encapsulation, placenta keepsakes and closing of the bones ceremony.
additional.p2: These services are created with the same intention as every part of Cora's care: to support the mother, honor what her body has carried, and create space for rest, nourishment, and emotional closure.

placenta.title: Placenta encapsulation
placenta.p1: Placenta encapsulation is a practice that may bring additional support for postpartum healing and recovery. These placenta capsules are taken during the postpartum chapter. Placenta encapsulation is available for both vaginal and cesarean births. It's also available for all birth places (hospital, home, birth center).
placenta.p2: The placenta is an organ your body grows with each pregnancy to sustain the new life growing inside. It brings oxygen and nutrients to baby and filters waste and much more.
placenta.p3: The placenta is packed with nutrients and minerals. There are some reported benefits to taking your placenta capsules such as:
benefits: May decrease the risk of "baby blues"
Replenishes depleted iron levels from birth
May increase milk production and supply
placenta.process: The process envolves cleaning, steaming, dehydrating and grinding the placenta before encapsulating. The capsules only hold placenta powder, with nothing additional, including no herbs or oils.
placenta.capsules: Capsules are clear and unflavored. Flavored capsules available upon request (for an additional charge)!
placenta.cord: Umbilical cord keepsakes are pending umbilical cord length.
placenta.print: Placenta prints can be done naturally or with edible food coloring. You get to choose your color!
placenta.tincture: A tincture has an infinite shelf life and can be utilized once your capsules are used up.
placenta.evidence: While there is limited research on the benefits of placenta consumption, some studies have been done. In 2016, two studies showed that the placenta contains 1/4 of the iron recommended for lactating women, plus traces of other minerals. They also found 15 hormones present in the placenta, with progesterone and estradiol at levels that could reach physiological effects. Further studies are still to be released, including a randomized trial on the potential effects on postpartum depression.

additional.packagesNote: All packages include placenta pick-up at your birth place (pending location) and drop off to your home (pending location). Mailing via priority shipping offered for locations outside of drop off zone.

closing.title: Closing of the bones - $275
closing.p1: Closing of the bones offers a time and space to honor your body for all it has done during pregnancy. In many cultures, women traditionally receive this care multiple times during the first 40 days after giving birth. Closing of the bones can also be done after loss, after transitioning or closing a chapter in your life (divorce, new job etc).
closing.p2: During the closing, rebozos are used to sway and rock certain points of your body before tucking the cloth underneath you. It can promote physical healing during the postpartum chapter by improving circulation, and may help with emotional and spiritual healing as well. It can be done at any point in your life, not just in the immediate postpartum period. You can still experience the benefits even 40 years postpartum! It is a space for you to be held, to honor your journey and your body. If desired, a castor oil pack can be placed on your lower abdomen to promote warmth and healing to your uterus, which can also be symbolic and healing if a hysterectomy has been done.
closing.p3: This service is available for an additional investment for families who choose in-home postpartum support.

points.title: Care for the new mother (whether this is your first or third baby).

story.title: Meet the heart behind Cora.
story.p1: Cora Perinatal Care grew from my own experiences with motherhood, my work supporting new mothers, and a deep belief that families deserve to feel cared for during one of life's biggest transitions.
story.p2: My name is Bruna Gomes. I am mother of three, a wife, a dog mom, and nature lover. I am passionate about helping families feel more prepared, informed, and supported as they enter parenthood. My own pregnancies, births, and postpartum experiences have taught me that every season is different. After a difficult postpartum experience following the birth of my third child, I sought out the support and resources I needed to find my way through it. That experience changed the way I saw postpartum care and deepened my desire to make sure other mothers don't feel like they have to navigate it alone.
story.p3: As a certified postpartum doula, a certified placenta specialist and an educator, my work focuses on helping families prepare for postpartum before they are in it, while also providing practical, compassionate support once they arrive there. I believe you don't need more pressure to have the perfect postpartum experience. My approach is simple: I want families to feel more prepared, more informed, and more supported. I want to be the calm person in the room who can offer practical help, answer questions without judgment, encourage rest, and remind you that needing care does not mean you are failing.
story.p4: My work is also deeply connected to my Brazilian roots and my experiences living between two cultures. Cora comes from coração, the Portuguese word for heart, and my logo's hibiscus flower is inspired by one of the flowers I love seeing when I'm in Brazil. Both are meaningful reminders of where I come from and the heart I bring into this work. I bring the warmth and leveza, or lightness, that I associate with my Brazilian culture together with the boundaries and intentional holding of space that have shaped my experiences in the United States. Together, these influences have shaped the way I care for families: with warmth, honesty, respect, and intention.
story.closing: At the heart of my work is a simple belief: you deserve to be cared for, too.

mission.title: Mission
mission.text: At Cora, our mission is to provide warm, practical, individualized support that helps families feel supported, informed, confident, and cared for throughout pregnancy and the postpartum period. Through education, hands-on support, and compassionate guidance, we create space for mothers and families to navigate this transition in a way that feels right for them. Cora is rooted in the belief that no family should have to navigate this season alone. Every service is offered with care, intention, and respect for each family's unique needs, experiences, and choices.

items.q: Do I need postpartum support if I have family nearby?
items.a: You can have family around and still need professional support. Loved ones often want to help, but they may not always have an unbiased perspective on how to support newborn care, feeding questions, recovery, rest, routines, or the emotional parts of postpartum. Cora's role is to bring calm, unbiased and practical guidance and help your support system work better for you.

items.q: What if I feel like I should be able to do this on my own?
items.a: Needing support does not mean you are not capable. It means you are moving through a major life transition and deserve care while you do it. Many mothers feel guilty receiving help, even when they deeply need it. Part of this work is helping you rest, receive support, and lean into your intuition.

items.q: Do you tell families what they should do?
items.a: No. Cora offers guidance, education, resources, and practical support, but your family's values and choices matter. The goal is not to impose one way of feeding, resting, parenting, or recovering. The goal is to help you feel informed and supported in the decisions that are right for you.

items.q: What areas do you serve in person?
items.a: In person support is available in the Boston area, Northern Massachusetts and Southern New Hampshire, depending on location and availability. For families outside the in-person service area, virtual support may be a good fit.

items.q: Can I work with you before the baby arrives?
items.a: Yes! Cora offers birth preparation, newborn care, lactation, and postpartum preparation. These sessions help you feel more prepared before baby arrives and give you a clearer sense of what support, recovery, feeding, and newborn life can look like.

items.q: Will I benefit from doula care even if this isn't my first baby?
items.a: Absolutely! At Cora, we provide support to families whether they are expecting their first baby, or have older children. Our belief is that every new mother and parent deserve to be cared for and supported, no matter how many times you have gone through it.

items.q: How do I know which service is right for me?
items.a: Start with the form. After you share a little about your needs, we can schedule a complimentary 15 to 30 minute call. During that conversation, we talk through where you are in your journey, what feels hard or unclear, and what kind of support would make the most sense for your family.

author.title: From Bruna
author.p1: Hi! I'm Bruna Gomes, a postpartum doula, educator, placenta specialist, mother of three, wife, and Brazilian-American living between two cultures in Massachusetts.
author.p2: I've experienced postpartum three times, and each season taught me something different about motherhood, recovery, and the kind of support we need along the way. During my third postpartum, I found myself searching for support and answers in the middle of the night. I wanted information that felt calm, honest, and grounded in real life, not advice that made me feel like I was falling behind.
author.p3: These notes come from what I've learned through all of my postpartum seasons, from motherhood, and from supporting real families through pregnancy and postpartum.
author.p4: No perfect postpartum here. Just honest information, practical support, and reminders of what you don't have to carry alone.
